changes.value:
# Fixture

What this project is, how it is built and checked, and the rules that apply
only here. Written in the project language by the orchestrator (or by the
only agent, when working alone). Filled in on the first capture
(`capture/initial.md`) and kept current by later ones.

## What it is

Describe the project here in one or two sentences.

## Map

The main components, where their code lives and who owns each one. One line
per component; detail goes in `domains/<COMPONENT>.md`.

| Component | Path | Owner | Card |
|---|---|---|---|
| | | | |

## Stack and environment

Languages, frameworks, package managers, runtimes and the tools an agent can
expect on the machine.

## Verification

The checks that must pass before work is called done:

```
# Add the type check, lint and test commands of this project here.
```

## Build and release

How the project is built and released, and who may release.

## Project rules

Rules that apply only to this project, each with its reason and date. A rule
here takes precedence over `RULES.md`.

## Traps

What cost a session once and will cost it again: the symptom, the cause and
how to avoid it. Search by keyword before touching an area.

# Current context

Short reading at the start of every session: one page (see the limit in
`kit.json`). It does not replace the canonical documents; it points at them.
Written by the orchestrator in the project language, when a priority, a risk
or an active rule changes.

Last review: 2026-10-28.

## Now

- Nothing in progress yet. The project is described in `PROJECT.md`; the
  first capture fills both files.

## Waiting on the owner

- None yet. Items waiting on the owner live in `plans/TRACKING.md`.

## Active risks

- None recorded yet.

## Decisions that shape the work

Only decisions every session must know, each with an id, date and reason,
for example "[D-1] 2030-01-10: uploads keep the old endpoint until 1.4,
because two clients still call it." Product detail belongs in `domains/` and
plans.
